description: Change a format this document **already** declares, as its table does: add `columns`, `claims`, `computed` columns, `unique`, `constraints`, `rollups` and `aggregates` as `declare_format` takes them; `rename`, `change` or `remove` what it has; `order` the columns. A rename keeps its values. Refused, naming the rows: a `required` column on rows, removing a column holding values, a list the rows do not fit, a type or unit change over values. Writes nothing until `commit: true`.

aggregates.description: New totals, as `declare_format` takes them. A `count` needs no `works_out`.

change.description: Columns it has, named, with what changes: `{ name, type: "enum", values }`.

claims.description: New claims, each with a `name`, an `expression` with one `=`, an optional `tolerance` and a `note` — as `declare_format` takes them.

columns.description: The new columns, after the ones it has. Up to 64. `text` — Words. A name, a note, a code — anything not measured. `integer` — A whole number, with no fractional part at all. `real` — A number that can have a fractional part. `date` — A day. No time of day and no timezone, ever. `boolean` — True or false, and nothing in between. `enum` — One of a list of words you write down here. Each value is any text — spaces, emoji, any language — listed once. A row may send any case; it is stored as written, and anything else is refused. `money` — An amount of money, in a currency the row names. Becomes two columns — minor units and a currency — so it is never a float. `link` — A row of another format. An equation here may read one column of the row it names, and no further. `quantity` — A figure and the unit that row is in — 150 g here, 200 ml there. Two columns. If every row shares one unit, a real with a unit is simpler. `decimal` — A number kept to a fixed count of places — a rate, a unit price. Needs a scale, the places it keeps (1 to 9). Written as a string, "3.5"; extra places are refused, never rounded. `month` — A month, as YYYY-MM. A period, not a day in it. `instant` — A moment, kept in UTC to the millisecond. Written with its offset — 2026-09-23T14:05:00Z. A time with no zone is refused. `links` — Several rows of another format, in order. Written as a list of row names or ids. An equation reads it only by an aggregate. `percent` — A share, shown as 12.5% — a VAT rate, a fee. Typed 87, "87%" or 0.87 — each 87%; 1 is 1%, "0.5%" half of one. Four places. A claim reads 0.87. `time` — A time of day, HH:MM — a shift start. Typed "09:30", "1430" or "2:30pm". end - start of two is hours, past midnight too. `enums` — Several of a list of words you write down here — tags, allergens. Written as a list — ["vegan", "quick"]. Each member is checked against the list, and one outside it is refused by name. `elsewhere` — A row in another document — its path, then the row’s name. Written "F:/projects/site/site.emd S1 U5". Never refused for being out of reach: read back, it says what the row holds now, or that it is unresolved. `file` — A file on this computer, by its path. Or a local app’s address; never http.

commit.description: Write it. Omit or false for the dry run.

computed.description: New computed columns, as `declare_format` takes them.

constraints.description: New row constraints, each `{ rule, note }` as `declare_format` takes them — refused, naming the rows, while any row already breaks one.

format.description: The format to change, by name.

order.description: Every column, new ones too, once each, in order.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

remove.description: Names of columns, claims, totals, computed columns, rollups or rule sets.

unique.description: Columns it already has that should become unique — refused, naming the repeated values, while two rows share one.

name: extend_format
title: Change a format
